result.title: Inferring Transferable Rewards via Active Inverse Reinforcement Learning
result.summary: Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) aims to recover expert rewards that transfer across environments with differing dynamics. Prior work has shown that such transfer is possible when gathering expert demonstrations across sufficiently different dynamics. In practice, however, expert demonstrations are costly, making it critical to select the right dynamics to reduce the quantity of expert data required for learning transferable rewards. We propose a two-phase approach: we first cycle through the available dynamics to obtain a reliable reward estimate, then actively select dynamics to reduce our uncertainty about the expert reward. Crucially, this yields novel sample complexity guarantees on transfer that hold for any dynamics, with a rate independent of the number of available dynamics. Empirically, our method significantly reduces the number of expert demonstrations needed to learn a transferable reward.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出两阶段主动逆强化学习方法：先在不同动力学环境中轮流采集以得到可靠奖励估计，再主动选择动力学以降低对专家奖励的不确定性，并给出与可用动力学数量无关的迁移样本复杂度保证。
AI.relevance_reason: 「主动选择最能降低不确定性信息来源」的表述，与 LVR 中视觉证据筛选及 LOOK/STOP 的收益-成本权衡在信息价值视角上可能相通，可作为形式化线索核查，但领域距离较远、尚需验证可迁移性。
